deities: Bhagavathy (Goddess, worshipped as the Supreme Mother; believed to be the deified Kannaki of the Silappathikaram)
festivals: Attukal Pongala (10-day festival in Kumbham, February-March; the Pongala offering on the 9th day draws millions of women and holds a Guinness World Record for the largest gathering of women for a religious festival)

history.dynasty: Uncertain/legendary; the temple is ancient and associated with the saint Chattambi Swamikal, who is said to have meditated on the premises
history.period: Ancient (no securely established founding date); the legend ties it to the Tamil epic Silappathikaram era
history.summary: The Attukal Bhagavathy Temple, about 2 km from the Padmanabhaswamy Temple, is one of South India's most revered Devi shrines and is popularly called the 'Sabarimala of Women'. Attukal Bhagavathy is believed to be the divine manifestation of Kannaki, heroine of the Tamil epic Silappathikaram: after destroying Madurai, Kannaki travelled through Kerala and rested at Attukal, and the temple's Thottampattu hymns sung during the festival narrate her story; her image also appears on the gopuram. The temple blends Kerala and Tamil architectural styles; the sanctum holds two idols of the Goddess - the original adorned with gold and gemstones. It is world-famous for Attukal Pongala, when millions of women cook the rice-and-jaggery offering in earthen pots across a ~5 km radius of the city. The government declares a holiday in the Trivandrum Corporation area on Pongala day.

name: Attukal Bhagavathy Temple
town: Thiruvananthapuram (Attukal locality, ~2 km from East Fort)
town_description: Thiruvananthapuram (Trivandrum) is the capital of Kerala, a coastal city built on seven hills at the state's southwestern tip. It is a historic administrative and cultural centre - seat of the Travancore royal family, major museums, the Kerala legislature, and the Technopark IT hub - as well as a beach destination (Kovalam, Varkala nearby). Attukal is an old residential quarter about 2 km southeast of the East Fort temple complex, famous as the seat of the Pongala festival that turns the whole city into consecrated ground.
